- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.67), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to avoid missing downward momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to forecast by subtracting 0.5–1.0x the recent sentiment swing.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ prices unless sentiment strongly signals reversal.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33–0.67 range, model tends to drift toward extremes; anchor forecast near 30-day moving average unless sentiment pushes otherwise.
